surprise.title: In Nassau, a free 13-minute walk leads to 65 steps carved by hand from solid rock
surprise.body: Your Legend sailing reaches Nassau on Thursday, December 17, and one of the best things there costs nothing. The Queen's Staircase is a walkway of 65 limestone steps, known locally as the 66 Steps because it originally had one more. Around 600 enslaved people carved it out of solid limestone between 1793 and 1794, working with limited tools, to cut a direct route from Fort Fincastle down to the town. It climbs a total of 102 feet up Bennet's Hill, the highest point in Nassau, with water cascading beside the steps into a pool and a shaded path between high stone walls and tropical trees at the bottom. In the 19th century it was named in honor of Queen Victoria. Tour guides like to say the 65 steps match the years of her reign, but that story is false, since she ruled a little under 64 years. It is about a 13-minute uphill walk from the pier, though the fort at the top is closed for restoration. Back home today looks dry and mild, about 59 to 69 degrees with sunset at 5:37 PM. Twenty days until you sail on December 13.
